chapter: Blackbirds, Carmen Jones and the Ziegfeld Follies
title: Talking pictures killed vaudeville and cut pay
summary: Sound films knocked out vaudeville and brought salary cuts; they were poorly paid but continued, even on Broadway, for peanuts.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: So you see, in this business, vaudeville -- talking pictures came in and that knocked vaudeville out. Then what can you do? Nothing. Trying to do something, they'll give you a job and try to cut your salary then on account of the pictures. I keep thinking that's on my neck. Try to find something to make a
living on then, talking pictures are going to cut out your chances then. So we tried everything we knew how.
Were you paid well? Were you paid well during vaudeville?

No, you don't get paid well -- well, what? How you know you got paid well. Today you get paid well, that's 25 years later or more. But in those days you didn't get paid well. You're lucky to get in the theater to play, let alone to get paid well.
What else could I do? What else could I do? I had made a name at this then. I got to take what follows or take nothing, some of the times it didn't work, couldn't work for the money.
But nonetheless you still worked on Broadway in that time.
Yeah, worked on Broadway but what was I getting? Oh, peanuts, I can't begin to tell you that.
